import numpy as np
import skimage as ski

cases = []

# Case 1: large constant int image (expected nan on buggy)
image1 = np.zeros((1080, 1920, 3), dtype=int)
B1 = ski.measure.blur_effect(image1)
cases.append(("zeros_1080x1920x3_int", B1))

# Case 2: ones scaled by factors along channel axis
factors = [0.0, 1.0, 2.5]
for factor in factors:
    image2 = np.ones((10, 10, 3), dtype=float) * factor
    B2 = ski.measure.blur_effect(image2, channel_axis=-1)
    cases.append((f"ones_10x10x3_factor_{factor:g}", B2))

# Case 3: broadcasted ramp (uniform/zero-variance along blur axis)
row = np.linspace(0, 1, 11)
# shape (10, 11)
image3a = np.broadcast_to(row, (10, 11))
B3a = ski.measure.blur_effect(image3a)
cases.append(("broadcast_row_shape_10x11", B3a))
# shape (4, 5, 6)
row6 = np.linspace(0, 1, 6)
image3b = np.broadcast_to(row6, (4, 5, 6))
B3b = ski.measure.blur_effect(image3b)
cases.append(("broadcast_row_shape_4x5x6", B3b))

# Summaries
vals = {name: float(v) if np.ndim(v)==0 else float(np.array(v).ravel()[0]) for name, v in cases}
nan_any = any(np.isnan(v) for v in vals.values())
nanmean = np.nanmean(list(vals.values())) if nan_any else float(np.mean(list(vals.values())))

# record scalars so comparison can detect nan vs 1.0
probe("nan_any", nan_any)
probe("nanmean", float(nanmean) if np.isfinite(nanmean) or np.isnan(nanmean) else nanmean)
for k, v in vals.items():
    probe(k, v)

# Also include a check value explicitly expected buggy: at least one of the cases should be NaN
# (zeros_1080x1920x3_int should be NaN on buggy).
